title: Bounded In-Memory Stream: Tumbling Windows with Late-Event Grace
description: Simulates a bounded in-memory event stream with tumbling windows; compares a no-grace baseline against a watermark-based grace period for handling late sensor readings.
novelty: Unlike the TF-IDF tool router (static text classification), this project simulates a temporal event stream requiring time-based windowing, watermark tracking, and late-event reprocessing—a fundamentally different algorithmic domain (single-pass stream computation vs. batch classification with train/test split).
method: Algorithm: watermark-based tumbling window processor with a grace period of 1 window_size; late events (event_time < watermark) within grace are re-inserted into their window and the aggregate is recomputed. Baseline: no grace—any event whose event_time falls below the current watermark is dropped permanently. Validation: deterministic in-memory replay of a seeded event stream sorted by arrival time; no train/test split (single-pass processing). Metrics: window_mean_mae (lower=better, MAE of per-window computed means vs ground-truth means), late_retention_rate (higher=better, fraction of late events successfully incorporated), max_window_skew (lower=better, max absolute difference between event count in computed vs true window).
acceptance_tests: make_dataset(seed=1, n_samples=64) and make_dataset(seed=2, n_samples=64) produce different X arrays (numpy assert_array_equal fails)
run_experiment algorithm metrics: late_retention_rate >= baseline late_retention_rate AND window_mean_mae <= baseline window_mean_mae (grace period must not worsen either metric)
